procure

/pruh-KYOOR/ - rhymes with secure · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Procure means to obtain, especially with care or effort.

For the school's new darkroom, Mr. Vann procured chemicals no supplier would ship to a private address.

Example

The request slip asked for a 1911 county atlas, out of print for a century. The librarian did not shrug it into the interlibrary queue; she set out to procure the thing, writing to two estate auctioneers, leaving her card with a map dealer in the next state, and cultivating a retired surveyor's widow for most of a year. When the atlas finally arrived — water-stained but whole — she set it on the counter like a landed fish.

Procure is the exact word for what she did, because procure means to obtain, especially with care or effort — the getting has a story. Get and obtain report only that the thing arrived; buy names nothing but the paying. Procure smells of legwork: letters written, favors banked, sources worked patiently until the thing is in hand.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

acquire: Acquire means to come to possess, by whatever route — purchase, gift, plain luck. It cares only that the thing is now yours. Procure cares how: the word carries the legwork, letters written and favors banked before the thing finally lands. Acquiring is the outcome; procuring is the campaign.

source: To source something is to find where it can be got — the supplier, the seller, the grower nobody else knows. Sourcing only finds the door; obtaining and procuring both end with the thing in hand, and procure adds that the getting itself took patient work.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

forfeit: give a thing up entirely

give up: let it go — or quit the hunt

Where it sits · how much effort the acquiring implies

get → obtain → procure

get vs. procure: Get is the plainest rung under procure — no effort implied, no story behind the getting at all.

obtain vs. procure: Obtain stops short of procure — a shade more formal than get, but still silent about effort; procure means the getting took work.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-: for, on behalf of

Root — cure: care (Latin cura)

Put it together: Pro- (on behalf of) + cure (care) = to take care of something for someone. Latin procurare meant to manage or look after; the caretaker who managed a household did its hard hunting for supplies, and English kept that half — obtaining as an act of care and effort.

Use the root in a new word: curator: A museum's curator is literally its caretaker — the same cura, spent on a collection instead of a shopping list.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / logistical

Procure is the quartermaster's verb: it flags that the getting was a project — calls made, sources hunted, favors spent. Obtain is the formal neutral; acquire cares only that possession arrived; get is the everyday floor. Reach for procure when the difficulty of the getting is the story, which is why armies and props departments live by procurement.
